node.title: Re^8: Text::CSV encoding parse()
node.author: Tux
node.doctext:
Using the perl internals through [metamod://Data::Peek]'s [https://metacpan.org/pod/Data::Peek#DPeek-($var)|DPeek], you'll see both versions if UTF-8 is in effect without the fragile use of utf8 function calls. It also shows the importance of using utf8 in your example code.

$ perl -MData::Peek -wE'my $data = "Euro symbol: € | I \N{U+2764}\N{U+FE0F} \N{U+1F42A}"; DPeek $data' PV("Euro symbol: \303\242\302\202\302\254 | I \342\235\244\357\270\217 \360\237\220\252"\0) [UTF8 "Euro symbol: \x{e2}\x{82}\x{ac} | I \x{2764}\x{fe0f} \x{1f42a}"] $ perl -Mutf8 -MData::Peek -wE'my $data = "Euro symbol: € | I \N{U+2764}\N{U+FE0F} \N{U+1F42A}"; DPeek $data' PV("Euro symbol: \342\202\254 | I \342\235\244\357\270\217 \360\237\220\252"\0) [UTF8 "Euro symbol: \x{20ac} | I \x{2764}\x{fe0f} \x{1f42a}"] $ perl -Mutf8 -MData::Peek -wE'my $data = "Euro symbol: \xe2\x82\xac | I \xe2\x9d\xa4\xef\xb8\x8f \xf0\x9f\x90\xaa"; DPeek $data' PV("Euro symbol: \342\202\254 | I \342\235\244\357\270\217 \360\237\220\252"\0)

Enjoy, Have FUN! H.Merijn
